Hi Jane,

Thanks again for taking the time to speak today — great conversation and helpful context on ACME's data residency and compliance needs. Quick recap and next steps on our end: 

- Redwood overview: hosted inference with optional dedicated/private deployments; we can scope out an architecture that keeps customer-controlled keys and data separation for regulated workloads.
- Compliance items you flagged: SOC 2 Type II status, data residency for EU workloads, and the vendor security questionnaire.

Action items I promised:
1) Share our current subprocessor list (attached CSV). It includes cloud infra, monitoring, and analytics vendors and a brief column on data access boundaries.
2) Provide our SOC 2 Type II summary and where to request the full report.
3) Kick off the vendor security questionnaire — happy to have David (security) join the next call for any technical questions.

I've attached a CSV with our subprocessors (redwood_subprocessors_20260620.csv) and a short SOC 2 summary (SOC2_TypeII_2025_summary.pdf). If you prefer, we can run a secure NDA/portal share for the full evidentiary report — link below.

Proposed next step: 30 min sync with your security team + David from Redwood. Are you available Tue/Wed morning PST?

Best,

Marissa,

Thanks — received both attachments and the recap. A few quick clarifying questions from our InfoSec side before we schedule the technical sync:

- Can you confirm which cloud providers host customer data in production (AWS/GCP/Azure)? We need region-level granularity (e.g., us-west1, eu-west2) for our data residency assessment.
- For the subprocessors listed, which ones have access to plaintext customer content vs. only metadata/telemetry?
- Do you offer customer-managed key (CMK) options for encryption at rest and an HSM/KMS integration?

Also attaching our initial vendor security questionnaire (acme_vendor_questionnaire_initial.pdf) — we completed the high-level sections and highlighted areas we need more detail on (data access, logging retention, incident response SLAs).

We can do a 30-min call; Tue at 09:30 PT would work for us. If David can join, that would be ideal.

Best,
Jane Park

ACME Corp
jane.park@acmecorp.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@acmecorp.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Subprocessor list & SOC 2 (post-demo)

Hi Jane — great, thanks for the quick turnaround and the questionnaire. Answering your bullets inline and next steps below.

- Cloud providers / regions: Production hosting primarily on AWS (us-west-2) with some services and optional GCP regions for multi-region failover (us-west1, europe-west2). We can pin EU-only hosting for customers requiring EU-only residency.

- Data access boundaries: The attached CSV includes an "access_level" column; summary below:
  - Storage & compute infra (AWS/GCP): can access ephemeral plaintext in-run for inference but no long-term retention of customer content by default.
  - Observability/monitoring vendors: have access to aggregated telemetry and anonymized traces; do not have access to raw customer prompts by default.
  - Analytics/BI partners: only access pseudonymized metadata unless otherwise contracted (we can negotiate restricted access on vendor-by-vendor basis).

- Encryption / CMK: Yes — we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and GCP KMS for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted customers we offer envelope encryption and can arrange bring-your-own-key under a contract clause.

SOC 2: the summary is attached; full Type II report can be shared under our secure portal or NDA. Link: https://secure.redwood.com/ndas/ND-78923 (we can generate a one-time access link for your team).

Proposed next steps:
1) David to join a 30-min technical sync to walk through the questionnaire gaps and access controls.
2) We'll upload a redacted copy of the full SOC 2 report to the secure portal and share a one-time link.
3) If helpful, we can provide a scoped subprocessor MSA clause and redline suggestions for ACME's legal team.

I'll send calendar invites for Tue 2026-06-22 09:30 PT unless you want a different slot.

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
